sources.citation: Pittayaporn, Pittayawat. 2009. The Phonology of Proto-Tai. PhD dissertation, Cornell University. xix+417 pp.
sources.note: Comparative reconstruction; Yooy appears only as language no. 68 in the Appendix data-source table (SWT; 'Southern Laos, relocated groups in central and northeastern Thailand'; source Boonsner 1984, cited as 'Unpublished M.A. thesis, Mahidol University, Nakhorn Pathom'). Stress is discussed only for Proto-Tai sesquisyllables (unstressed minor + stressed major syllable); no Yoy-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: บัญญัติพร สมบัติเมืองกาฬ (Banyatpoon Sombatmangkan). 1990. ภูมิศาสตร์ภาษาจังหวัดสกลนคร: การศึกษาโดยใช้ศัพท์ [Linguistic geography of Sakon Nakhon province: a lexical study]. MA thesis, Silpakorn University. 139 pp.
sources.note: Scan without text layer, not scanned. Abstract (read on the SURE repository page) says it maps where Nyo, Phu Thai, Kaloeng and Yoi (Yoy) are spoken in Sakon Nakhon using 30 lexical items; a lexical-geography study, not a phonological description.

sources.citation: Phakkahn, Naiyapak. 2017. Phonology and Grammar Sketch of Yoy. MA thesis, California State University, Long Beach. 138 pp. ProQuest 10638626; ISBN 9780355575484.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Silent on Yoy word stress. Chapter 2 (pp. 8-41) covers consonants, vowels, five tones (2.4) and word/syllable structure (2.5: words of 1-3 syllables, every syllable bears a tone, checked vs unchecked syllables); no stress/accent/prosody statement. The only occurrences of 'stress' are a paraphrase of Enfield on LAO reduplication ('the first syllable becomes unstressed, while the second syllable bears all the stress and tone', p. 51) and Payne's generic definition of compounds ('may include a stress pattern', p. 46) — neither is a claim about Yoy.

sources.note: English article gives consonants, vowels and five tones 'according to Phakkahn (2017)' (cited via academia.edu/35702725); no mention of stress. Thai article has no phonology.
